summary: In November 2025 the Shenzhou-20 crew (commander Chen Dong) were about to leave China's Tiangong space station when, during final checks, Chen Dong spotted what looked like a leaf on the return capsule's window. It was a set of cracks, most likely from an impact by a tiny piece of space debris, and later the crew said some cracks had penetrated through the outer pane. The 5 November return was postponed; on 14 November the crew came home in the Shenzhou-21 capsule instead, leaving the newly arrived Shenzhou-21 crew without a safe ride home. China launched the uncrewed Shenzhou-22 around 25 November 2025 as a replacement lifeboat, carrying a porthole crack repair device; a spacewalk in December photographed the damage, and Shenzhou-20 returned uncrewed on 19 January 2026. A similar lifeboat swap happened on the ISS in 2022-23 when Soyuz MS-22 sprang a coolant leak and Soyuz MS-23 was launched empty to replace it. The lesson: crewed stations depend on always having a healthy lifeboat docked, and debris risk is growing. Shenzhou-24, scheduled for 25 November 2026, carries Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali as the first foreign visitor to Tiangong.
audience: Curious adults 18-45 who like engineering, space and near-miss stories

facts.fact: During final checks before the planned 5 November 2025 return, Shenzhou-20 commander Chen Dong noticed damage on the return capsule window; his first thought was that a small leaf had stuck to the outside.
China's space agency postponed the return because of a suspected space-debris impact and said the window glass had a crack that failed the requirements for a safe crewed return.
facts.source: CMSA statements via PBS NewsHour / AP (Nov 2025)

facts.fact: Examined under a microscope, the window showed several relatively long cracks and a shorter one, and the crew later said some of the cracks had penetrated through.
Sources disagree on the size of the debris: one report says under 1 mm, while an expert quoted by Scientific American speculated it could be 1-10 cm; what hit it is not known.
On 14 November 2025 the Shenzhou-20 crew returned to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-21 spacecraft, leaving the damaged Shenzhou-20 docked in orbit.
facts.source: PBS NewsHour; Space.com; The Register (14 Nov 2025)

facts.fact: That left the Shenzhou-21 crew aboard Tiangong temporarily without a crewed return vehicle.
China launched Shenzhou-22 uncrewed around 25 November 2025 (sources give 24 or 25 November) as a replacement return vehicle; it carried a porthole crack repair device.
In early December 2025, astronauts on a spacewalk took high-resolution photos of the cracked window.
The damaged Shenzhou-20 capsule returned to Earth uncrewed, landing at the Dongfeng site in Inner Mongolia on 19 January 2026.

A similar lifeboat swap happened on the International Space Station: Soyuz MS-22 developed a coolant leak in December 2022, and Soyuz MS-23 was launched uncrewed in February 2023 to bring its crew home.
Shenzhou-24 is scheduled to launch on 25 November 2026 from Jiuquan with Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong.
facts.source: Hong Kong Free Press (24 Nov 2026); Nature

facts.fact: Ali is expected to stay about a week and return on Shenzhou-23, while one Shenzhou-23 astronaut stays for a year-long mission.
facts.source: Hong Kong Free Press; Wikipedia: Shenzhou 24

avoid: Saying the crew was in immediate danger of dying; they were never stranded without options for long and no one was hurt
Stating a debris size as fact (sources disagree)
Saying Shenzhou-24 launched or docked before it is confirmed
Political framing (space race, military) or speculation beyond official statements
Calling Ali the first Pakistani in space (Namira Salim flew suborbital in 2023)
